metadata.purpose: Evidence-bounded nutrition, sleep, recovery, injury-risk, and supplement guidance for HYROX planning agents

evidence_labels.HYROX_DIRECT: Official HYROX standards or research in HYROX athletes/simulated HYROX settings.
evidence_labels.TRANSFER_EVIDENCE: Research from adjacent endurance, resistance, concurrent-training, or athlete populations; useful but not proven specifically in HYROX.
evidence_labels.COACH_PRACTICE: A bounded method from a credentialed coach or athlete transcript; never causal proof or a universal rule.
evidence_labels.CLINICAL_REFERRAL: Topic requiring a qualified clinician, registered dietitian, or sports-medicine professional rather than agent prescription.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Extended high-intensity exercise exceeding approximately 60 minutes can challenge fuel and fluid regulation; carbohydrate intake during the session is a test-in-training option rather than a mandatory HYROX rule.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: For sessions and races likely to exceed 60 minutes, ask whether the athlete has previously tolerated carbohydrate during running/erg/station work. If not, propose a low-risk practice trial and record GI response rather than assigning a fixed dose.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not state that every HYROX athlete requires a specific grams-per-hour target or that any intake guarantees performance.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Total daily nutrition and appropriately distributed protein are more important than a rigid post-workout anabolic window; rapid carbohydrate restoration matters most when a demanding session follows within about four hours.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: When two demanding sessions are close together, flag recovery fueling as a planning consideration. Otherwise prioritize regular meals, adequate energy availability, and dietitian-guided personalization.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not diagnose low energy availability, prescribe calorie floors, or require immediate post-session supplements.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Athletes should trial race food and fluid in training or simulated competition before race day.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Include an optional fueling-practice note in longer simulations and record food, fluid, timing, and GI tolerance.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not make a commercial gel, drink, or product brand part of the plan.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Athlete sleep needs and responses to sleep interventions are individual; habitual short sleep below seven hours/night is a recognized marker of sleep inadequacy, but a universal sleep-duration target is not ideal.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Ask the athlete to monitor a simple 7-14 day sleep trend. If sleep is repeatedly curtailed or sleep quality is poor, reduce optional training stress and surface a coach-review flag.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not prescribe a universal 9-hour target, diagnose insomnia, or claim that one poor night requires an automatic missed session.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Long-term sleep behavior, sleep education, screening, and management of travel/competition risks are supported practical priorities; consumer wearables have measurement limitations.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Use self-reported sleep and a wearable only as trend inputs. Offer low-impact alternatives or extra recovery time after a pattern of poor sleep, especially before high-intensity or high-impact work.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not interpret a wearable sleep score as a clinical diagnosis or objective clearance to train.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Load management combines progressive overload, specificity, variation, individuality, recovery, and avoidance of prolonged underloading; it is not synonymous with rest.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Progress one primary variable at a time where possible (volume, density, load, or race specificity), include lower-stress sessions, and compare athlete response to prior weeks.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not use a single ACWR cutoff, a fixed 10% rule, or a single biomarker to predict injury or automate a medical decision.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Strength-training interventions reduced sports injuries in a meta-analysis, but the trials were not HYROX-specific and do not specify a universal program for hybrid racers.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Retain appropriately dosed strength work for tissue capacity and movement quality, while adjusting it around high-impact running and station sessions.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not claim that strength training prevents a particular injury or prescribe return-to-sport criteria after injury.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Deloading practice is common in strength sports, but the research is observational and not HYROX-specific.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Present a planned or response-based lower-stress week as an adjustable option when fatigue, joint soreness, life stress, or performance trend warrants review.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not mandate a universal deload calendar or presume a fixed volume reduction is superior for every athlete.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Only a small number of supplements have good evidence for specific use contexts; individual responses vary and all competition-use protocols should be trialled in training.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: Provide a neutral evidence-and-risk discussion only after the required inputs are known. Encourage qualified professional review and batch-tested products for athletes subject to anti-doping rules.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not recommend a supplement as required, prescribe doses to minors, make disease claims, or make performance guarantees.

evidence_bounded_guidance.claim: Caffeine, creatine, nitrate, and buffering agents are examples discussed in the IOC consensus, but their benefit, safety, timing, and legality depend on the individual and scenario.
evidence_bounded_guidance.operational_use: If the user explicitly asks, expose a medical/dietitian review checklist and race-practice reminder rather than creating a mandatory protocol.
evidence_bounded_guidance.do_not_infer: Do not stack stimulants, recommend unverified products, or treat supplement marketing as evidence.
